skill.name: file-header-guardian
skill.description: Guides AI coding agents to add concise @input, @output, and @pos header comments to new or changed code files.
skill.summary: Adds consistent file header contract comments for code files.
skill.author: Dimon94

security_audit.summary: All seven static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences in SKILL.md. The skill provides file header comment templates and exemptions, with no evidence of command execution, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Teams lose context when source files lack clear purpose and dependency notes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to add concise header comments for supported code files.
actual_capabilities: Provides @input, @output, and @pos header templates for TypeScript and JavaScript files.
Provides a Python docstring template for the same file contract fields.
Provides a shell comment template for script files.
Reminds agents to update the file header and the directory CLAUDE.md after changes.
Lists exemptions for config files, style files, generated declarations, and node_modules.
limitations: Does not include executable validation or formatting scripts.
Does not automatically infer accurate dependencies without project context.
Does not cover every language or generated file type.
Instructions are primarily written in Chinese.

use_cases.title: Standardize New Services
use_cases.description: Add purpose and dependency notes when creating new application service files.

use_cases.title: Review Documentation Drift
use_cases.description: Check that file headers still match behavior after code changes.

use_cases.title: Keep Agent Work Traceable
use_cases.description: Help AI coding sessions leave concise context for future maintainers.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Header
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a new file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create this source file and add the required @input, @output, and @pos header comment before the implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing Header
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt after changing a file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this changed file and update its header comment so the dependencies, exports, and system role are accurate.

prompt_templates.title: Check Exemptions
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for mixed file changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these changed files and add headers only where the skill applies. Skip config, style, generated, and dependency files.

prompt_templates.title: Synchronize Local Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this feature folder, update applicable file headers, and align the related directory CLAUDE.md notes with the current file roles.

output_examples.input: A new user service file is created without a header.
output_examples.output: The response adds a concise header that names the database dependency, service operations, and module role.

output_examples.input: A modified Python module now calls a cache helper but the header is old.
output_examples.output: The response updates the dependency note and keeps the module purpose aligned with the implementation.

output_examples.input: A change set includes a stylesheet, a generated declaration file, and a shell script.
output_examples.output: The response skips exempt files and adds the contract header only to the script file.

best_practices: Write headers after understanding the real dependencies and exported behavior.
Keep each header short enough to maintain during normal code review.
Update directory documentation when file roles change materially.
anti_patterns: Do not add generic headers that restate the filename only.
Do not force headers into exempt generated, config, style, or dependency files.
Do not leave the header unchanged after changing dependencies or module responsibility.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It only provides documentation templates and workflow instructions.

faq.question: Which file types are shown in the templates?
faq.answer: The skill includes examples for TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and shell files.

faq.question: Can it decide every dependency automatically?
faq.answer: No. The agent still needs project context to write accurate @input notes.

faq.question: Should generated files receive headers?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly exempts generated declaration files and dependency directories.

faq.question: How does it relate to CLAUDE.md?
faq.answer: It reminds agents to keep file headers and related directory documentation synchronized.

faq.question: Is this useful outside Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance can also help Claude and Codex maintain consistent file documentation.
